body.evidence: primary = mean(GAUC, nDCG@5) is invariant to per-user monotone shifts, so the pointwise loss spends capacity on calibration that the metric ignores. The seed's own docs state no pairwise path exists and that writing one is a legitimate hypothesis.
body.hypothesis: The champion optimises pointwise logloss while it is scored on within-user ordering; a within-user BPR pairwise objective (positive vs negative impression of the SAME user) removes the need to model user-level base rates and should raise both GAUC and nDCG@5 substantially.
body.mechanism: model.py gains step_bpr: for a batch of (pos_row, neg_row) index pairs it computes z+ , z- via the existing logits(), sets g = -sigmoid(-(z+ - z-))/B on the positive rows and +that on the negative rows, and reuses _apply with the stacked design matrix (the shared-embedding gradient path is unchanged). train.py gains a sampler that uses group_bounds() to build, per epoch, one pair for every positive impression of each user with a uniformly drawn negative from the same user (users with no mixed labels are skipped). config.json loss = 'bpr'. Early stopping and train_subset scoring are unchanged.

reflection.next_question: Is the remaining headroom representational rather than objective — i.e. does adding genuine feature interaction capacity (an FM/embedding-dot term in model.py over user x item-side fields, trained under the now-validated BPR objective) move dev primary by more than the ~0.002 the loss change bought, and does it lift nDCG@5 rather than only GAUC? Run this as the mandated architecture change, with a cheap first sweep of pairs_per_pos in {4,8} folded in so the objective is not left under-sampled while the representation question is being asked.
reflection.prediction_comment: Direction correct, magnitude badly over-forecast: predicted +0.012, realised +0.0017 (14% of forecast), and it failed its own +0.006 success bar. First calibration point of the run and it is an overconfident one — file it as evidence that mechanism-plausibility arguments in the objective_loss lane were not translating into effect-size discipline. Future estimates in this lane should be shrunk toward the 0.001-0.003 band unless a structural reason for more is given.
reflection.remaining_uncertainty: Whether the BPR gain is under-exploited rather than exhausted: pairs_per_pos was 1, only 382k pairs/epoch, and the whole fit used 14.7 s of the 600 s allowance — 4-8 negatives per positive with light L2 and a longer schedule could plausibly extract another 0.001-0.003 from the same objective. Also unresolved whether the gain concentrates in users with many impressions (BPR sampling favours them) or is uniform; and whether GAUC moving 2.5x more than nDCG@5 means the improvement is in mid-list ordering that the top-5 cut mostly ignores, which would matter for where to aim next.
reflection.what_happened: The BPR candidate ran clean (14.7 s of a 600 s budget, 11 epochs, dev peak at epoch 7) and scored a signed dev primary of 0.603387 — a new champion, +0.001691 over the pointwise seed and +0.001787 over the published baseline. The learning curve is sane and monotone-early (0.5936 -> 0.6034 by epoch 7, then decay), so the sign convention and the duplicated-row np.add.at accumulation are correct. Component metrics: GAUC 0.667382 -> 0.669797 (+0.00242), nDCG@5 0.536011 -> 0.536978 (+0.00097). The harness-computed train/dev gap fell sharply, 0.0852 -> 0.0520, with train primary dropping 0.6869 -> 0.6553: the pairwise objective genuinely stopped spending capacity on per-user calibration and memorisation, but the freed capacity bought far less ranking than predicted.
reflection.why: The mechanism is confirmed in kind but refuted in magnitude. The stated causal story — pointwise logloss wastes capacity on user base rates that a shift-invariant metric ignores — makes two predictions, and the diagnostic one is strongly borne out: train primary fell 0.031 while dev rose, i.e. the model stopped fitting exactly the component the metric discards, and the train/dev gap contracted by 39%. But the payoff prediction (+0.012, success bar +0.006) missed by ~7x; the realised +0.0017 is below the run's epsilon of 0.002. That combination is informative rather than ambiguous: objective misalignment was real and is now largely spent, so it cannot have been the dominant term in the 0.601 -> 0.848 oracle gap. body.hypothesis: The champion uses only 5 categorical fields (user_id, video_id, author_id, tab, dur_bucket) and therefore has almost no content or context signal; adding the pre-impression columns the loader actually carries (user profile attributes, video attributes, time-of-day/date context) as extra encoded fields will raise dev primary by more than any further loss engineering.
body.mechanism: With only ids + tab + duration bucket, the FM can only generalise across items through the author_id and dur_bucket slots. KuaiRand rows carry additional pre-impression descriptors (e.g. user activity/profile columns, video type/upload type/music id, duration, hourmin, date). Encoding those as further fields gives shared parameters that transfer to sparsely-observed video_ids, which is exactly where within-user ranking of tail impressions currently fails. Implementation: enumerate data.columns at fit time, auto-select columns that are (a) low-to-moderate cardinality or bucketable and (b) on an explicit pre-impression whitelist, bucket continuous ones by train-only quantiles, and append them to cfg['fields'].
